stem.en: Madar and dandelion seeds carry fine, fluffy hairs. What kind of seed dispersal does this suit best?

feedback.en: Yes. Light seeds with fine hairs stay in the air and drift.
Fluffy hairs help a seed stay up in air. They are not needed for floating.
Fine hairs slow the fall, so the seed drifts away from the parent.
These seeds are carried through the air, and soil has no part in that.

explanation.en: Fine hairs make these seeds light and slow to fall, so moving air can carry them far from the parent plant.

hints.en: What can lift something very light?
Think of a seed drifting past on a breezy day.
